paragraphs: I got into cybersecurity because I like figuring out how things work, and how they break. Right now I'm doing that as a Student SOC Analyst at Old Dominion University, where I spend my shifts triaging phishing, digging into risky sign-ins, and chasing down endpoint alerts in CrowdStrike, QRadar, and Entra ID. There's nothing quite like tracing a weird alert back to a real campaign.

At home, I run a Raspberry Pi honeypot that attackers poke at every day, and I'm building a Python-based mini SIEM to make sense of what they're trying. This summer I also taught at ODU's CyberAI Summer Camp, which reminded me how much I enjoy explaining security in a way that clicks for people.

Before cyber, I spent years in customer-facing roles and freelance live sound engineering. Those taught me how to stay calm under pressure and communicate clearly, both of which come in handy when an incident hits.

I'm Security+ certified, studying for the CCNA, and pursuing a B.S. in Cybersecurity with a Political Science minor (graduating December 2027). I'm especially interested in SOC and GRC roles in the Hampton Roads defense community. Outside of work, I'm into OSINT and national security policy, live sound, and speedcubing.
U.S. Citizen · Eligible for Secret clearance
